main_text.p: rum conjuncta atque unita proprio suo corpori, in quo vixerat {2}. Qui porrò ultimo illo die superstites erunt, nequaquam morientur more reliquorum, sed in momento & jactu oculi, immutabuntur, à corruptione videlicet in incorruptam naturam. Tunc aperientur libri ( nimirum conscientiae ) & mortui judicabuntur secundum ea, quae in hoc mundo egerint, sive bona sive mala. Quinetiam tunc redditurí sunt homines rationem de omni verbo otioso, quod locuti fuerint, etsi id mundus nunc pro ludo & joco reputet. In summa omnis tunc hominum hypocrisis & abstrusa quaeque cordis corum palam coram omnibus detegentur. Ac propterea sola judicij istius memoria impijs & reprobis merito est horrenda & formidabilis: pijs vero & electis summe exoptanda, & ingentis consolationis. Tunc enim redemptio ipsorum plane perficietur, & suavissimos laborum & dolorum suorum, quos in hac vita pertulerunt, fructus, consequentur: innocentia ipsorum tunc aperte ab omnibus agnoscetur, ipsique vicissim horrendam vindictam conspecturi

page.notes: Footnote mark "2" after "vixerat" has no matching note on this page; faint marks at the bottom left are not legible and are not transcribed. Line 1 begins with the fragment "rum" continued from the previous page. Italics in the "Tunc aperientur" and "redditur" passages are taken from the scan; "redditurí" is printed as "redditurí" with a faint accent-like mark, possibly a printing error for "reddituri". Paragraph breaks are not visible in the scan; the text is set as one unbroken paragraph. The final word "conspecturi" is split by the hyphen; the catchword "cturi" is recorded at the foot. "fuavissimos" and "viciffim" are printed as "fuavissimos" and "viciffim"; u/v and long-s normalised to "suavissimos" and "vicissim".
